solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Queen Victoria & Albert are absorbing the terrace

indicators.note: the Victoria and Albert letters take the queen's letters into their middle

parts.note: V, as in the V&A museum's initial
the ampersand is read as the word and
A, the other initial of the V&A
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A grand tableau of the royal couple taking over a terrace, perhaps at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria & Albert suggests the royal pair, but here it is the London museum known as the V&A, split into its initials and the ampersand.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed terrace or porch along the side of a house.

clue.text: For Hardy Evening outside church official wrong-footed Laurel?

indicators.note: the poetic evening word wraps around the official

parts.note: E'EN is the poetic contraction of evening found in Thomas Hardy's verse

indicators.note: the foot, the last two letters, of the official's title is set the wrong way round

parts.note: a verger looks after a church and leads processions

explanation.surface: A Laurel and Hardy gag: the church official tripped up by Laurel on an evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy are bait: Hardy is the poet who wrote E'EN, and laurel is the shrub. 'wrong-footed' swaps the closing ER of VERGER to make VERGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurel is a shrub that keeps its leaves all year, an example of an evergreen; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Obsessive rewriting new entry in yearbook

indicators.note: the abbreviation for new makes its entry into the middle of the obsessive word

parts.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, means fussily obsessive

explanation.surface: A fussy editor keeps rewriting a fresh entry in the school yearbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting' only colours the picture; the work is N going into ANAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a record of one year's events, the sort of chronicle a yearbook keeps.

clue.text: Wanting an evenly expressed poet

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the little word an goes missing

parts.note: andante is a musical direction for playing at a steady walking pace
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet whose verse is delivered in a flat, even voice is found wanting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly expressed' sounds like a description of the poet; it is the musical term ANDANTE, which loses AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet who wrote the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Bowl a ball Rob Key plays and misses opening for England B

indicators.note: the cricketer's name is shuffled while losing some letters, a batting term doing double duty
the opening of England is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Commentary on a former England batsman, Rob Key, swishing at a delivery in a second-string England B match.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E and B from ROBKEY and rearrange ROKY. To play and miss is a cricket batting failure; to york is to bowl a yorker, a ball pitched at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket to york a batsman is to bowl them a yorker, a delivery landing right at the feet.

clue.text: Location for war meeting that's close to consecration point after extremists disappear

indicators.note: the outermost letters of the combined phrase vanish

parts.note: by means near or close to
the altar is where the bread and wine are consecrated

explanation.surface: A church service where the priest stands near the altar as the zealots slip away.
explanation.walkthrough: BY ALTAR loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1945 Yalta Conference was where Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin met to plan the end of the Second World War.

clue.text: Demanding large starters make cook fry bacon and black ginger?

definitions.text: Demanding large starters make cook fry bacon and black ginger?

parts.words: Demanding large starters make cook fry bacon and black ginger?
parts.note: large starters are capital initials: Cook, Fry, Bacon, Black and Ginger then become famous people sharing one name, as surname for the dancer and first name for the rest

explanation.surface: A greedy diner insists the cook fries up bacon and black pudding with ginger.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised, the names give Roger Cook, Roger Fry, Roger Bacon, Roger Black and the dancer Ginger Rogers.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Cook, Roger Fry, Roger Bacon and Roger Black are all Rogers, and Ginger is a Rogers too.

clue.text: Father and No 1 brother

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
A is first-class, number one

explanation.surface: A family ranking: father and the eldest brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Fra is the Italian title for a friar, meaning brother, as in Fra Angelico.

clue.text: Forte beginning for what's not initially a summery Glyndebourne?

parts.note: f is the musical marking for forte, loud

indicators.note: the first letter of the summery word is dropped

parts.note: aestival means belonging to summer

explanation.surface: A musician wonders how to start loud at a summer opera event at Glyndebourne.
explanation.walkthrough: AESTIVAL (also spelt estival) loses its opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Glyndebourne is an English summer opera festival, held in Sussex; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Question Inland Revenue about spouting drivel on English monarch

indicators.note: about signals rearranging the tax office's letters, and spouting has the letters of drivel ejected from them

explanation.surface: A taxpayer quizzes the Inland Revenue, Britain's old tax office, about its nonsense on an English king.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the UK tax authority. 'spouting' ejects the letters of 'drivel' from it, and 'about' rearranges the remaining NANENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Anne reigned over England, Scotland and Great Britain from 1702 to 1714.

clue.text: Taking the second note needs quite a bit of paper

indicators.note: taking means taking away, so the note is removed from the verb

parts.note: requires means needs
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale, do re mi

explanation.surface: Taking up music theory needs a fair stack of manuscript paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' looks like adding a note but means removing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper, so several of them make quite a bit.

clue.text: Losing half its red and blue bits, new Google design?

indicators.note: new signals the letters left are made into a fresh arrangement
losing has letters dropped from the company name

parts.words: half its red and blue bits
parts.note: the company's ... colours its two g's blue and its o and e red; one of each colour goes

explanation.surface: A query whether Google's redesign drops some of its trademark coloured letters.
explanation.walkthrough: GOOGLE loses one blue G and the red E, and GOOL is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is a company's emblem, a graphic design standing for the brand.

clue.text: Roman poet's sex with exciting girl

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A racy line on a Roman poet's love life with a thrilling girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is not English here but the Latin for six, and 'Roman' nudges toward the Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil wrote the Aeneid and is Dante's guide through the underworld.

clue.text: Brut was traditional line

parts.note: ex means former, what something was
trad is a short form of traditional, as in trad jazz
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Remarks on a brand of champagne that used to be a classic line.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut and extra-dry are both labels for dry styles of champagne.

clue.text: Forever English, in this respect

indicators.note: in this says the letters sit inside the words just given

explanation.surface: A patriotic claim that Englishness endures forever in a given way.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to hold someone in deep respect or awe; here a verb meaning the same.

clue.text: Gasbag sometimes caught on bicycle in Calais gym

parts.note: en vélo is French for by or on bicycle, Calais being a French port
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A cyclist in a French gym caught on a bike while a windbag talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' hints that envelope's first syllable is sometimes said the French way, as 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The envelope of a balloon or airship is the fabric bag that holds the gas.

clue.text: Plan to make second-in-command third-in-command?

definitions.meaning: taking away a vice-captain's rank, a jokey verb for demotion

explanation.surface: A scheme for demoting the deputy one rank down the chain of command.
explanation.definitionFit: A device is a plan or scheme devised to bring something about.

clue.text: Diameter = 27

parts.note: d is the usual symbol for diameter
the equals sign is read as is

explanation.surface: A geometry formula setting a diameter equal to twenty-seven.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 points to the answer at 27 across, the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and in Dante the city of lower Hades bears that name.

clue.text: In pow-wow about private area of W1

indicators.note: the talk word goes around the little word in

parts.note: a pow-wow is a talk or chat
own means private, one's own

explanation.surface: Native American talks over a secluded spot in London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: W1 is the London postcode district covering Soho, where London's Chinese quarter lies.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Chinese quarter lies around Gerrard Street in Soho, in the W1 postal district.

clue.text: Form of entertainment served up in illusory democracy

indicators.note: served up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Political satire: a sham democracy put on as a show for the public.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' reads the hidden letters from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is a genre of entertainment meant to make people laugh, and Dante's poem is called the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Scoundrels of old church body in Kansas

indicators.note: the church part sits in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: Historic villains found among a Kansas congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: Knave is an old-fashioned word for a dishonest rogue.

clue.text: Provided assistance through west side of the capital

indicators.note: the help word runs through the trimmed city name
the west side of the word is its left-hand half, so its right half goes

parts.note: London is the UK capital
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: Aid routed through the western boroughs of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid on means supplied or arranged, as when a host lays on food.

clue.text: Long to drink Beaujolais, possibly the best

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so the wine goes inside

parts.note: to be dying for something is to long for it
Beaujolais is an example of vin, French for wine

explanation.surface: A wine buff yearning for Beaujolais, perhaps the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine is used colloquially for excellent, supremely good.

clue.text: To quit beer and spirits, sweet, jump on board!

parts.note: to kick a habit is to quit it
a flip is a hot drink of beer and spirits sweetened with sugar

explanation.surface: A drinker gives up booze and is told to hop on the wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickflip is a skateboarding trick, a leap in which the rider flips the skateboard beneath them.

clue.text: It's the end, we hear, that Allen key's locked up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top
locked means held inside the words of the tool's name

explanation.surface: A DIY lament: the Allen key, a hex wrench for flat-pack furniture, has been put away out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' belongs to the definition: a knell is the tolling bell people hear at a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the solemn tolling of a bell marking a death or ending.

clue.text: Musical heroine shows us a leg

parts.note: per means a or each, as in once a day
leg and on are the same side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cheeky leading lady flashing a leg at the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The on side of a cricket field is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva Perón is the title character of the musical Evita.

clue.text: My way to penetrate layer!

indicators.note: the road word gets inside the bird

parts.note: a hen is a layer of eggs
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a way

explanation.surface: A cry of joy at finding a route through a stratum of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum but is a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavens! and My! are both mild exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: Feel swell? Yes and no

definitions.meaning: to rise and fall with the swell of the sea
to retch: to make the motion of vomiting, which is being sick and not being sick at once

explanation.surface: Asked whether they feel fine, a seasick passenger answers ambiguously.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is both to rise and fall like waves and to retch without bringing anything up.

clue.text: Road about marshy area

parts.note: the M1 motorway is Britain's best-known road
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A road skirting a stretch of wetland.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mire is a stretch of swampy ground, a bog.

clue.text: Suffering guy unhappy with "remarkable" parrot

indicators.note: unhappy and the quoted remarkable, re-marked or set down afresh, together say the man and bird are rearranged

explanation.surface: A miserable man with a supposedly amazing talking bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator spans 'unhappy with "remarkable"', wrapped between the two fodder words GUY and PARROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Purgatory is a place or state of torment, and Dante's second realm of the afterlife.

clue.text: This may mislead Klingon, say, getting out of his skin

indicators.note: shedding the skin means losing the outer letters

parts.note: a Klingon is a Star Trek alien

explanation.surface: A sci-fi scene: a Star Trek Klingon shedding his skin to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is designed to deceive, so it may mislead.

clue.text: This man is going to ruin

parts.note: he refers to a man
'll is the contraction of will, is going to

explanation.surface: A prediction that a certain man is headed for disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to the dogs is to go to ruin, and the underworld of the damned stands for utter ruin.

clue.text: Is this 27? (Conclude it's not)

parts.note: to infer is to conclude from evidence
no is the denial that it is not

explanation.surface: A question whether this is 27 across, and a bracketed verdict that it isn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across is the answer HELL; the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy is named for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is Italian for the underworld of the damned, and the title of Dante's first canticle.
